transcript.text: Thanks everyone for joining. As we discussed, the replayable webhook service is planned for production enablement next Monday. I've reviewed the current draft of the operating policy — 100 webhook requests per minute per tenant, 8 replay workers, 30-day payload body retention, and no targeted customer notice. Before I sign off on this policy, I want to follow our standard round-robin review. Could reliability and customer success each state any final operational or customer commitments they see, or any concerns with the policy as drafted?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to raise a customer commitment concern before sign-off. I confirmed with account managers yesterday that exactly 2 named enterprise tenants have signed webhook terms requiring payload retention to be set at exactly 7 days — the draft's 30-day retention must be reduced to exactly 7 days to match those contractual terms. The same terms also require advance notice to those 2 tenants before the service is enabled. Providing that notice immediately would satisfy the requirement for next Monday's enablement. I finished reconciling the account list after the policy draft was circulated and hadn't yet posted the result in the launch channel, so I'm raising it now.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to raise a capacity-review commitment before sign-off. While tuning an unrelated queue dashboard this morning, I found that the reserved production capacity can support the webhook service only with a per-tenant limit of exactly 60 requests per minute and exactly 3 replay workers. The draft's 100 requests per minute and 8 replay workers would exceed the reservation. I haven't updated the policy ticket yet, but before sign-off, a capacity-review commitment is required to document the adjusted rate limit and worker count against the reservation.
transcript.speaker: A2
